title: AXM Infinite Fabric
description: A source-bound demonstration program for the First Charter Tiny World, its generated revisions, playable trials, durable memory, provider boundaries, and portable custody.

evidence.title: First Charter Tiny World
evidence.claim: The demonstration begins from the real creator-owned Tiny World constructor and sealed world revision.

evidence.title: Semantic action transaction
evidence.claim: The First Star is collected through the same schema-bound semantic action path used by play.

evidence.title: Board, Map, Planet, and Play parity
evidence.claim: Every projection reads the same stable cells, entities, law binding, and append-only ledger.

evidence.title: Bounded Infinite Fabric patch
evidence.claim: Generation output is constrained to known data operations and cannot carry arbitrary canonical runtime code.

evidence.title: North village proposal
evidence.claim: The village proposal is a real structured patch compiled against the current world revision.

evidence.title: Accepted immutable revision
evidence.claim: Only the host acceptance transaction may materialize the proposal and append its attributable event.

evidence.title: First Charter Classic Trials
evidence.claim: The montage runs the same five Canvas game engines exposed by the playable Classic Trials product.

evidence.title: Durable world memory
evidence.claim: Collected objects, accepted patches, completed trials, and consequences retain stable identities and attribution.

evidence.title: Replaceable generation providers
evidence.claim: Providers may propose bounded content but cannot become law, ledger authority, or a dependency during play.

evidence.title: Portable showcase package
evidence.claim: The static product, capture outputs, program, receipts, and SHA-256 ledger are assembled and verified together.

evidence.title: Presenter control qualification
evidence.claim: A browser transaction traverses the actual world, patch, game, memory, provider, and custody stages without page errors.

evidence.title: Demonstration authority boundary
evidence.claim: The demonstration does not issue human enjoyment, live-provider generation, household hardware, or product acceptance.

chapters.title: One world. Every game. Still yours.
chapters.body: The First Charter begins as a creator-owned cartridge and becomes a living planet, a game suite, and a persistent memory without surrendering custody to a model or platform.

chapters.title: Board, Map, Planet, and Play are the same world.
chapters.body: Every projection reads the same stable entities, law binding, relationships, quests, and append-only event ledger.

chapters.title: Describe a place. Receive a bounded proposal.
chapters.body: Generation providers propose structured cells, entities, assets, and known behaviors. They cannot rewrite law, inject canonical runtime code, or mutate the ledger directly.

chapters.title: The village becomes part of the running world.
chapters.body: A new cell, bridge, shopkeeper, and quest appear through a content-addressed revision while the previous world remains recoverable.

chapters.title: A story can contain an entire game shelf.
chapters.body: Five recognizable arcade forms become chapters of The First Charter. Their victories restore seals and alter the same Tiny World memory.

chapters.title: Play leaves durable marks on the world.
chapters.body: Collected objects, completed trials, relationships, accepted patches, weather, and bridge state remain attributable across every projection.

chapters.title: Models compete. The world does not move.
chapters.body: Muse, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, local models, voxel generators, splats, and future systems all meet the same bounded world and asset contracts.
chapters.claim: SAME PATCH CONTRACT · PROVIDER ABSENT DURING PLAY

chapters.title: Export the branch. Kill the network. Keep playing.
chapters.body: The world package carries its accepted revisions, behavior identities, assets, controls, and memory. The originating provider is provenance, never a runtime dependency.
chapters.claim: PROVIDER OFF · NETWORK OFF · WORLD CONTINUES
